FINAL ENTERPRISE QA — IVX AUTONOMOUS + IVX IA SENIOR DEVELOPER

Execute on the EXISTING IVX Holdings production project only.

Do not create a new application.
Do not create a new repository.
Do not create a second Render service.
Do not create demonstration data.
Do not bypass failed tests.
Do not mark PASS based on variable presence, UI cards, plans, or narrative.
Do not start the next gate until the current gate is VERIFIED PASS.

==================================================
ENTERPRISE QA MODEL
==================================================

Use the same operating principles used by large-scale software organizations:

1. Every code change passes automated gates.
2. High-risk actions require owner approval.
3. Tests run before merge and after deployment.
4. Mobile testing runs on real devices.
5. Deployments are controlled and reversible.
6. Retries are bounded and idempotent.
7. Failures preserve evidence and never become fake PASS.
8. Production monitoring verifies the real user experience.
9. Every completed autonomous job has immutable evidence.
10. A human owner retains final control of production changes.

==================================================
QA EXECUTION RULE
==================================================

Execute the gates strictly in this order:

GATE 1 — Production identity
GATE 2 — Build and static analysis
GATE 3 — Automated test foundation
GATE 4 — Owner authentication and security
GATE 5 — Autonomous task creation
GATE 6 — Queue and worker execution
GATE 7 — Approval enforcement
GATE 8 — GitHub code-change workflow
GATE 9 — Render deployment workflow
GATE 10 — Live production verification
GATE 11 — IVX IA Chat reliability
GATE 12 — Chat-to-autonomous integration
GATE 13 — Restart, retry, and recovery
GATE 14 — Mobile real-device QA
GATE 15 — Performance, load, and stability
GATE 16 — Final owner-controlled end-to-end job

For every gate:

1. Inspect.
2. Test.
3. Record failure.
4. Identify root cause.
5. Fix the root cause.
6. Commit the fix.
7. Deploy when required.
8. Repeat the failed test.
9. Attach real evidence.
10. Mark VERIFIED PASS or VERIFIED FAIL.

Stop after each gate and return its evidence.
Do not combine unverified gates.

==================================================
GATE 1 — PRODUCTION IDENTITY
==================================================

Confirm the exact production system.

Required:

- GitHub owner
- repository
- branch
- GitHub HEAD SHA
- Render service name
- Render service ID
- Render live SHA
- Render deployment ID
- production API URL
- IVX IA Chat URL
- Supabase project reference
- EAS project ID
- Android application ID
- iOS bundle ID
- AWS account masked
- AWS region
- S3 bucket masked
- CloudFront distribution masked

Call:

GET https://api.ivxholding.com/health

Required response:

- HTTP 200
- service name
- environment
- version
- commit SHA
- build timestamp
- boot timestamp

Required equality:

GitHub HEAD SHA = Render live SHA

Failure conditions:

- wrong repository
- wrong branch
- old live commit
- duplicate production service
- domain pointing to the wrong backend
- health endpoint without real deployment metadata

Do not continue until Gate 1 passes.

==================================================
GATE 2 — BUILD AND STATIC ANALYSIS
==================================================

Run from a clean checkout of the production branch:

- dependency installation
- lint
- formatting validation
- TypeScript typecheck
- unused-code detection
- dependency vulnerability scan
- secret scan
- production build
- Expo configuration validation
- API build
- database migration validation

Required:

- no ignored type errors
- no build-time secret exposure
- no missing imports
- no unresolved modules
- no duplicate route registration
- no stale environment-variable fallback
- no hardcoded production credentials

Return:

- command
- start time
- finish time
- exit code
- error count
- warning count
- artifact generated
- PASS/FAIL

Do not continue until the production build succeeds cleanly.

==================================================
GATE 3 — AUTOMATED TEST FOUNDATION
==================================================

Create or verify real tests for:

UNIT TESTS

- task state transitions
- approval validation
- authentication helpers
- retry calculations
- idempotency key generation
- message normalization
- upload validation
- deployment status parsing
- provider response parsing
- permission checks

INTEGRATION TESTS

- API plus Supabase
- API plus queue
- queue plus worker
- worker plus approvals
- worker plus GitHub
- worker plus Render
- chat plus task creation
- task plus progress events
- attachment plus storage
- owner authentication plus protected routes

END-TO-END TESTS

- owner login
- owner creates task
- task enters queue
- worker processes task
- approval is requested
- approved action executes
- progress appears in chat
- completion evidence persists

Required test behavior:

- deterministic
- repeatable
- isolated
- no fake provider responses in production verification
- explicit timeout
- cleanup after test
- stable test identifiers

Create a test inventory containing:

- test ID
- feature
- test type
- expected result
- actual result
- duration
- evidence
- status

==================================================
GATE 4 — OWNER AUTHENTICATION AND SECURITY
==================================================

Test on Android, iOS, and web:

1. Manual owner login.
2. Invalid password rejection.
3. Empty-field validation.
4. Non-owner rejection.
5. Owner route access.
6. Admin Hub access.
7. Autonomous dashboard access.
8. Variables module access.
9. IVX IA Chat access.
10. Logout.
11. Login again.
12. Session persistence after app restart.
13. Token refresh.
14. Expired-token rejection.
15. Revoked-token rejection.
16. Backend restart while logged in.
17. MFA optional from Settings.
18. No forced MFA unless enabled by owner.

API security tests:

- request without JWT → 401
- invalid JWT → 401
- valid non-owner JWT → 403
- valid owner JWT → 200
- service token used only for permitted internal actions
- authorization checked server-side
- no trust in client role values

Audit:

- hardcoded secrets
- secret logging
- public owner routes
- missing RLS
- service-role leakage
- unauthenticated worker endpoints
- cross-user message access
- cross-user attachment access

==================================================
GATE 5 — AUTONOMOUS TASK CREATION
==================================================

Create one production-safe read-only request from IVX IA Chat:

“Audit current production health without modifying code or data.”

Prove:

- chat message saved
- owner identity recorded
- task ID created
- request body stored
- risk level assigned
- required approval scope calculated
- initial status stored
- creation timestamp stored
- audit event created

Required task statuses:

- CREATED
- VALIDATING
- QUEUED
- RUNNING
- WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL
- TESTING
- DEPLOYING
- LIVE_VERIFYING
- COMPLETED
- FAILED
- CANCELED

Invalid state transitions must be rejected.

==================================================
GATE 6 — QUEUE AND WORKER EXECUTION
==================================================

Verify the real queue and worker.

Test:

1. Task enters queue.
2. Worker heartbeat is active.
3. Worker claims the task once.
4. Worker lock has an expiration.
5. Another worker cannot execute the same task.
6. Job state is stored in Supabase.
7. Progress events are written.
8. Worker completion is recorded.
9. Job remains visible after restart.

Required worker evidence:

- worker ID
- task ID
- job ID
- claimed_at
- heartbeat_at
- attempt number
- lock expiration
- current phase
- last completed action
- final status
- traceId

No dashboard card is accepted as proof without database and log evidence.

==================================================
GATE 7 — APPROVAL ENFORCEMENT
==================================================

Verify these scopes:

- READ_ONLY
- GITHUB_WRITE
- DEPLOY
- DATABASE_WRITE
- STORAGE_WRITE
- SECURITY_CHANGE

Tests:

1. Read-only approval cannot change code.
2. GitHub approval cannot deploy automatically unless DEPLOY is approved.
3. Deploy approval cannot alter database data.
4. Expired approval is rejected.
5. Canceled approval is rejected.
6. Approval from another user is rejected.
7. Approval for another task is rejected.
8. Single-use approval cannot be reused.
9. Approval cannot expose credentials.
10. Every approval use creates an audit event.

Every approval must contain:

- approval ID
- owner ID
- task ID
- scope
- issued_at
- expires_at
- used_at
- status
- action fingerprint

==================================================
GATE 8 — GITHUB CODE-CHANGE WORKFLOW
==================================================

Execute one harmless approved code change.

Recommended safe change:

Add a non-sensitive field to /health:

autonomousQaVersion

Required flow:

1. Request GITHUB_WRITE approval.
2. Validate approval.
3. Confirm correct repository and branch.
4. Capture parent SHA.
5. Create clean working state.
6. Modify the intended file only.
7. Display the diff.
8. Run lint.
9. Run typecheck.
10. Run tests.
11. Run production build.
12. Commit.
13. Push.
14. Read the commit back from GitHub.
15. Store the new SHA in task evidence.

Reject the job if:

- wrong repository
- dirty unrelated files
- tests fail
- approval expired
- merge conflict exists
- secret appears in diff
- production build fails

Required evidence:

- repository
- branch
- parent SHA
- new SHA
- files changed
- insertions
- deletions
- tests executed
- approval ID
- push result

==================================================
GATE 9 — RENDER DEPLOYMENT WORKFLOW
==================================================

Execute only after Gate 8 passes.

Required:

1. Request DEPLOY approval.
2. Confirm exact Render service.
3. Confirm no deployment is already active.
4. Trigger one deployment.
5. Capture deployment ID.
6. Follow build status.
7. Capture real build logs.
8. Confirm container boot.
9. Confirm health check.
10. Confirm worker heartbeat.
11. Confirm new SHA is live.

Do not trigger repeated deployments while one is active.

Deployment must fail honestly when:

- build fails
- pre-deploy fails
- health check fails
- wrong commit is deployed
- container crashes
- service cannot load required variables

Required equality:

GitHub new SHA = Render live SHA

==================================================
GATE 10 — LIVE PRODUCTION VERIFICATION
==================================================

After deployment, test the live production system.

Required live operations:

- /health → HTTP 200
- owner authentication → HTTP 200
- unauthenticated protected request → 401
- non-owner protected request → 403
- Supabase read
- Supabase controlled write and cleanup
- GitHub authenticated read
- Render service read
- AWS STS GetCallerIdentity
- S3 safe write/read/delete
- CloudFront asset request
- AI provider test
- worker job-status request with correct authentication

Variable presence alone is not proof.

Each provider test must include:

- timestamp
- operation
- HTTP status
- latency
- traceId
- masked identity
- actual result
- verdict

==================================================
GATE 11 — IVX IA CHAT RELIABILITY
==================================================

Test Android, iOS, and web.

MESSAGE TESTS

- send 1 message
- send 10 rapidly
- send 100 in a controlled conversation
- reconnect network
- restart app
- restart backend
- reopen conversation
- load older messages
- switch between conversations

Required:

- no missing messages
- no duplicates
- no incorrect ordering
- stable message IDs
- stable conversation IDs
- correct sender
- correct timestamps
- pagination works
- realtime reconnect works
- retry does not duplicate
- unread counts are accurate

COMPOSER TESTS

- keyboard does not cover input
- send button remains visible
- multiline input works
- scrolling remains stable
- draft behavior is correct
- Android Back works
- iOS safe area works
- mobile web works

ATTACHMENT TESTS

- image
- multiple images
- video
- PDF
- document
- failed upload
- canceled upload
- interrupted upload
- app restart during upload

Required:

- real progress
- clear failure
- stable attachment ID
- preview
- authorization
- no orphan files
- upload record linked to message

==================================================
GATE 12 — CHAT-TO-AUTONOMOUS INTEGRATION
==================================================

Send through IVX IA Chat:

“Run a production-safe health audit and return verified evidence.”

Prove the complete link:

chat message
→ request classifier
→ owner validation
→ task
→ job
→ queue
→ worker
→ provider checks
→ progress events
→ final task state
→ final chat response

Every autonomous chat response must display:

- task ID
- job ID
- current state
- completed steps
- real percentage
- last action
- next action
- blocker
- approval needed
- traceId
- final evidence

The AI must not claim completion unless the linked task is COMPLETED.

==================================================
GATE 13 — RESTART, RETRY, AND RECOVERY
==================================================

Run controlled failure tests:

1. Restart worker during a job.
2. Restart Render during a job.
3. Temporarily disconnect Supabase.
4. Simulate GitHub timeout.
5. Simulate Render timeout.
6. Simulate AI provider timeout.
7. Expire an approval.
8. Disconnect chat realtime.
9. Cause a controlled test failure.
10. Cancel a queued job.

Required recovery behavior:

- task state preserved
- no duplicate execution
- safe retry
- exponential backoff
- jitter
- maximum attempt count
- dead-letter status
- clear final error
- owner notification
- resumable job when safe
- manual intervention when unsafe

All mutating actions require idempotency keys.

The same task retried twice must not:

- create two commits
- trigger two simultaneous deploys
- send duplicate final messages
- upload duplicate files
- apply the same database mutation twice

==================================================
GATE 14 — MOBILE REAL-DEVICE QA
==================================================

Test on actual supported devices:

ANDROID

- current APK/AAB
- low-memory device
- current Android version
- older supported Android version
- cellular connection
- weak network
- background and foreground
- cold start
- warm start

IOS

- current production build
- current iOS
- older supported iOS
- cellular connection
- weak network
- background and foreground
- cold start
- warm start

Required:

- no crash
- no white screen
- no infinite spinner
- no keyboard overlap
- no lost owner session without cause
- no lost messages
- no duplicate tasks
- no stale autonomous progress
- correct deep links
- attachments work

Record:

- device
- OS
- app version
- build number
- test
- result
- screenshot/video
- crash log
- timestamp

==================================================
GATE 15 — PERFORMANCE, LOAD, AND STABILITY
==================================================

Execute controlled load levels:

- 10 concurrent users
- 100 concurrent users
- 1,000 simulated users

Do not claim 10,000 or 100 million readiness without infrastructure and test evidence.

Test:

- login
- chat send/read
- conversation load
- task creation
- worker polling
- provider status
- attachment metadata
- health endpoint

Measure:

- p50 latency
- p95 latency
- p99 latency
- error rate
- timeout rate
- CPU
- memory
- database connections
- queue depth
- worker utilization
- message duplication
- crash rate

Stability tests:

- 30-minute IVX IA Chat session
- 2-hour autonomous job-monitoring session
- repeated app background/foreground
- repeated network switching
- backend restart

Set explicit initial acceptance targets:

- health availability during test: at least 99.9%
- API error rate: below 1%
- duplicate task rate: 0%
- duplicate message rate: 0%
- lost completed-job evidence: 0%
- unauthorized production mutations: 0%

==================================================
GATE 16 — FINAL OWNER-CONTROLLED END-TO-END JOB
==================================================

Send this exact request through IVX IA Chat:

“Audit production, identify one safe defect, request the required approvals, fix it, test it, commit it to my GitHub repository, deploy it to the existing Render service, verify the live commit, and return all evidence here.”

Required sequence:

1. Owner message persisted.
2. Owner identity verified.
3. Task created.
4. Risk classified.
5. Read-only audit completed.
6. Defect identified with evidence.
7. GITHUB_WRITE approval requested.
8. Approval granted and validated.
9. Code fixed.
10. Diff recorded.
11. Lint passed.
12. Typecheck passed.
13. Tests passed.
14. Production build passed.
15. Commit pushed.
16. DEPLOY approval requested.
17. Deployment triggered once.
18. Render build completed.
19. New container booted.
20. /health returned HTTP 200.
21. GitHub SHA matched Render live SHA.
22. Provider tests passed.
23. Final task status became COMPLETED.
24. Final response appeared in IVX IA Chat.
25. Evidence survived app and backend restart.

==================================================
AUTONOMOUS DASHBOARD REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Display real database-backed information only:

- queued jobs
- active jobs
- waiting approvals
- testing jobs
- deploying jobs
- live-verifying jobs
- completed jobs
- failed jobs
- canceled jobs
- worker heartbeats
- queue depth
- provider status
- GitHub commits
- Render deployments
- retry history
- dead-letter jobs
- owner approvals
- two-hour reports
- daily reports

Every job must display:

- task ID
- job ID
- owner
- assigned agent
- request
- risk
- approval scopes
- status
- progress based on completed steps
- start time
- last heartbeat
- duration
- attempt count
- commit SHA
- deployment ID
- traceId
- evidence
- final verdict

No static, sample, seeded, or calculated fake values.

==================================================
MANDATORY DEFECT REGISTER
==================================================

For every defect discovered, record:

- issue ID
- gate
- severity
- affected platform
- reproduction steps
- expected result
- actual result
- root cause
- file/service/table
- fix
- commit SHA
- deployment ID
- retest evidence
- final status

Severity:

P0 — security breach, data loss, production unavailable
P1 — owner login, deployment, autonomous execution, or chat broken
P2 — major function degraded
P3 — minor defect
P4 — cosmetic issue

P0 and P1 defects block release.

==================================================
FINAL RELEASE DECISION
==================================================

Release status may only be one of:

VERIFIED PASS
- all critical gates pass
- no open P0/P1
- final end-to-end job passes
- live SHA matches GitHub
- evidence is complete

CONDITIONAL PASS
- no P0/P1
- limited P2 defects documented
- owner explicitly accepts risk

VERIFIED FAIL
- any critical gate fails
- evidence missing
- deployment SHA mismatch
- owner authentication fails
- autonomous execution is not persistent
- chat loses or duplicates messages
- security controls fail

UNKNOWN
- testing was not completed
- evidence cannot be retrieved
- provider access is unavailable

Never convert UNKNOWN into PASS.

==================================================
FINAL REPORT FORMAT
==================================================

Return:

1. Production identity
2. Gate results 1–16
3. Test totals
4. Passed tests
5. Failed tests
6. Open P0/P1/P2 defects
7. Autonomous worker status
8. IVX IA Chat status
9. Mobile-device results
10. Provider matrix
11. GitHub evidence
12. Render evidence
13. Recovery evidence
14. Performance evidence
15. Final end-to-end job evidence
16. Final release decision

For each gate show:

- status
- tests executed
- tests passed
- tests failed
- issue IDs
- commit SHA
- deployment ID
- evidence links or references
- timestamp

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
==================================================

Do not declare IVX IA Senior Developer autonomous until:

- it works without the owner keeping the screen open
- jobs persist across restarts
- tasks are never executed twice
- approval scopes are enforced
- secrets remain protected
- failures are reported honestly
- retries are bounded and idempotent
- code changes reach the owner’s GitHub
- deployments target the existing Render service
- GitHub SHA equals live SHA
- /health returns HTTP 200
- IVX IA Chat shows real task progress
- messages remain ordered and persistent
- Android, iOS, and web pass
- final owner-controlled job completes end-to-end
- evidence remains available after restart

Start with Gate 1 only.

Return the Gate 1 evidence and stop.
Do not start Gate 2 until Gate 1 is VERIFIED PASS.
